parole.testo: From German Autismus; likely entered through French autisme or English autism.

parole.significato: a block (building material such as a brick, concrete block, or cinder block)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Block. Semantic loan from French bloc in the sense "bloc" and semantic loan from English block in the senses "city block" and "set of sheets of paper".

parole.significato: chlorine (a toxic, green, gaseous chemical element (symbol Cl) with an atomic number of 17)
parole.testo: Likely via German Chlor or French chlore, from English chlorine, itself derived from Ancient Greek χλωρός (khlōrós, “pale green”) + -ine. Compare also Yiddish כלאָר (khlor), Polish chlor and Russian хлор (xlor) for the phonetic influence.
From German Matrize, itself from French matrice, from Latin matrix. Compare also Russian матрица (matrica), Polish matryca.
Coined by Joseph Klausner from עֹפֶרֶת (oféret, “lead”), by analogy with German Bleistift and French plombagine.

parole.significato: cartel (group of businesses or nations that collude to fix prices)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Kartell, from French cartel.
